children: US STOCKS START NEW WEEK IN THE GREEN AS CRUDE DIPS, TREASURY YIELDS EASE
Wall Street burst from the gate on Monday in a buying mood, as crude prices dipped below $100 per barrel, and Treasury yields easing across the curve.
All three major US stock indexes are green.
Fears that unchecked AI could be an existential threat to humanity were put on the back burner, with chipmakers
outperforming, giving the Nasdaq
the early edge.
Frontrunners so far also include communication services
with an assist from Meta
, which is rising 7.5% after Wells Fargo hiked its price target for the stock. Airlines (.SPCOMAIR), are also off to a good start.
On the other end of the scale, economically sensitive Dow Transports
are off 1%, along with energy
stocks , down 2%, falling in tandem with crude.

Crude prices touched an 11-day low in advance of the upcoming UN meeting, which could result in diplomatic progress in the Iran war. A partial recovery in Saudi oil shipments also calmed supply jitters.

With war-related energy price pressures morphing into broader, systemic inflation—which has prompted global central banks, including the Fed, to hike interest rates—equity markets have tended to move in opposition to crude since US and Israeli forces attacked Iran February 28, resulting in the closure of the crucial Strait of Hormuz.
Market-moving catalysts were scarce on the first day following Fed week. No economic data to speak of.
Later in the week, Flash PMI, new home sales, durable goods and consumer sentiment will round out a data-light week.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, speaking with reporters after an event in London, said that if today's inflation were demand-driven, it would require a more aggressive policy stance, and dismissed the idea of cutting interest rates as means to ease the US debt/deficit burden.
Here's where things stood as of 10:07 EDT:
Main US equity indexes green; Nasdaq out front
Comm Services lead S&P sector gainers; Energy weakest group
Europe's STOXX gains ~0.9%
Dollar gains; bitcoin rallies >5%; gold off ~1%;  US crude down >4%
US 10-year Treasury yield dips to ~4.97%
